# Aventura — Javadoc audit

*[Version française](JAVADOC_AUDIT.fr.md)*

*October 2026. Scope: the Javadoc generated by `mvn javadoc:javadoc` (`target/reports/apidocs`), the sources in
`src/main/java` (101 files, 19 packages) and the configuration of the `maven-javadoc-plugin` in `pom.xml`.*

The goal is to make the Javadoc **the reference of a 3D rendering engine API**: a user should be able to discover
the engine, write a first scene and extend the engine (shape, material, light, view) without opening the code. The
project already has almost all the content needed, in the README, `DESIGN.md`, `GEOMETRY_COOKBOOK.md` and
`BACKLOG.md`: most of the work is **bringing it back into the Javadoc, at the right place**, rather than writing it.
The identifiers (J1, S2, C3…) are used again in the roadmap of §7.

## 0. Summary

**The problem is not first a lack of comments, it is their form.** All the classes are commented, but the
generated Javadoc is hard to read for four reasons, all of which can be fixed mechanically:

1. **The MIT license is in the Javadoc comment of 100 classes out of 101.** Javadoc takes it for the description of
   the class: in **every** summary table (package pages, index, "All Classes"), the first sentence displayed is
   `------------------------------------------------------------------------------ MIT
   License Copyright (c) 2016-2026 Olivier BARRY…`. This is what makes the documentation look "not presentable".
   Fixing this single point already changes the look of the whole site.
2. **No home page, no package description.** No `overview.html`, no `package-info.java` (0 out of 19): the index
   page is a raw list of 19 package names, without a sentence, an example or a reading order. The demos
   (`com.aventura.demo`) appear at the same level as the API.
3. **The comments are written as plain text, not as Javadoc.** 0 `{@link}`, 0 `{@code}`, 0 `<p>` in the whole of
   `src/main`. The dashed lists, the line breaks and the **6 ASCII diagrams** (pipeline of `RenderEngine`, view
   volume of `Perspective`, `Torus`, `SpotLight`…) are merged into a single unreadable paragraph, and the class names
   they mention are not clickable.
4. **The configuration hides all the problems**: `<doclint>none</doclint>`, `<failOnError>false</failOnError>` and
   `<quiet>true</quiet>`. A run with `-Xdoclint:all` reveals **72 errors and 1,148 warnings**.

Only then comes the coverage: **43% of the public or protected methods and constructors** have a comment, and some
packages that matter most to the user are poorly documented (`model.world` 15%, `model.world.shape` 21%,
`model.light` 38%, `context` 39%).

There is good news too:

- The content already exists, often excellent: the package and option tables of the README, the architecture, the
  extension points and the conventions of `DESIGN.md`, the contracts C1 to C10 of the cookbook, and the API traps
  noted in `BACKLOG.md`.
- The examples are **already compiled and tested** (`HelloAventura`, `PyramidFrustum`, `ClosedConeFrustum`,
  `StreetLamp` in `src/test/java`): with `{@snippet}` (Java 18+, the project is on Java 21), the Javadoc can include
  them without copy and paste, and they will never get out of date.
- The math library (`math.vector`, 70%) and `tools.color` (88%) are already well commented.
- The links to the Javadoc of the JDK are already generated automatically (`java.awt.Color`, `Object`…).

**Estimated effort**: about 1 day for a result that is already presentable (phases 0 and 1), then 3 to 5 days spread
over time for a Javadoc at the level of a "public API" (phases 2 and 3).

## 2. Generation settings (J)

### J1. Take the license out of the Javadoc comment — **priority 1**

In each file, the MIT header and the description of the class share the same `/** … */` block. They must be
separated: the license in an ordinary `/* … */` comment at the top of the file (before `package`, the usual
convention), the description alone in the `/** … */` above the class.

```java
/*
 * MIT License
 * Copyright (c) 2016-2026 Olivier BARRY
 * ...
 */
package com.aventura.engine;

import ...;

/**
 * The core of the Aventura rendering pipeline: renders a {@link World} seen through a {@link Camera}...
 *
 * @author Olivier BARRY
 */
public class RenderEngine {
```

The 100 files have the same structure (the license between two lines of dashes, then the description): a small
script can make the change safely, and `git diff` can check it. The license does not need to appear in the Javadoc:
it is in the footer (J2) and in `LICENSE.md`.

### J2. Fix the footer

By default the plugin adds `Copyright © 2016–2026. All rights reserved.` to every page, which **contradicts the MIT
license**. To be replaced, for example by:

```xml
<bottom><![CDATA[Copyright &#169; 2016&#x2013;2026 Olivier Barry.
  Released under the <a href="https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT">MIT License</a>.]]></bottom>
```

### J3. Turn doclint back on, step by step

Today `doclint none` hides the 72 errors. Proposal in two steps:

1. `<doclint>all,-missing</doclint>`: all the checks **except** the missing comments. The 72 errors can be fixed in
   half a day (§4, C1); then `failOnError` stays `true`, so that they do not come back.
2. Once phase 3 is done: `all`, with `failOnWarnings` in continuous integration.

Also remove `<quiet>true</quiet>` during the work: the messages are the task list.

### J4. Presentation options

| Option | Proposed value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `<overview>` | `src/main/javadoc/overview.html` | home page (S1); the plugin already looks in `src/main/javadoc` |
| `<groups>` | see S3 | group the 19 packages by role |
| `<excludePackageNames>` | `com.aventura.demo` | the demos are not the API (or a separate "Demos" group, at the end) |
| `<additionalOptions>` | `--snippet-path ${project.basedir}/src/test/java` | tested examples (C4) |
| `<docfilessubdirs>` | `true` | images in `doc-files` (S4) |
| `<author>` | `false` | `@author` on 82 classes tells nothing to the reader of a single-author API |
| `<show>` | `protected` (unchanged) | needed for the extension points; but see A3 for the fields |
| `<doctitle>` | `Aventura ${project.version} — pure Java 3D rendering engine` | |

## 3. Structure: overview, packages, groups (S)

### S1. A home page (`overview.html`)

This is the first page one sees. It can take the beginning of the README almost as it is:

- the tagline ("A lightweight software 3D rendering engine, 100% pure Java…") and the Earth and Moon image;
- **Hello, Aventura**: the complete program, included by `{@snippet class=com.aventura.demo.HelloAventura}` from
  `src/test/java` (it is already compiled and produces the image of the gallery);
- "The scene and the engine": `RenderEngine` + `World` + `Camera` + `Lighting` + the two contexts, with the diagram
  of the pipeline (S4);
- a **reading order**: "Start with `RenderEngine`, then `World` and the shapes, then `RenderContext`";
- the table of the extension points of DESIGN §9, with `{@link}`s;
- the conventions of DESIGN §12 (Z up, direction of the directional lights, S → R → T order): information the user
  needs **before** writing a first scene;
- links to DESIGN, the cookbook and the GitHub repository to go further.

### S2. A `package-info.java` per package

19 short files (5 to 20 lines). The first sentence is displayed in the tables: it must say **what the package is
for**, from the point of view of the user. The content is already in the "Packages" table of the README and in
DESIGN §2. Example:

```java
/**
 * Built-in shapes ({@link Box}, {@link Sphere}, {@link Torus}, {@link Trellis}...) ready to be added to a
 * {@link com.aventura.model.world.World World}.
 *
 * <p>Every shape is a {@link com.aventura.model.world.GenerativeElement GenerativeElement}: its constructor
 * stores the parameters, and {@code build()} generates the vertices, the triangles and the normals.
 * To write your own shape, see the contracts on {@code GenerativeElement} and the
 * <a href="https://github.com/obarry/Aventura/blob/master/docs/GEOMETRY_COOKBOOK.md">Geometry Cookbook</a>.
 *
 * <img src="doc-files/cookbook_gallery.png" alt="Built-in shapes">
 */
package com.aventura.model.world.shape;
```

For `com.aventura.engine`, the package-info is the right place for "One frame, step by step" (DESIGN §4) and the
coordinate spaces; for `model.light`, the table of the kinds of lights (DESIGN §6); for `context`, the tables of
options and presets of the README.

### S3. Group the packages by role

Today the index shows 19 packages in alphabetical order (`context` first, `view` last). With `<groups>`, the index
follows the layers of DESIGN §2:

| Group | Packages |
|---|---|
| **Scene API** — build and render a scene | `engine` (for `RenderEngine`), `context`, `model.world`, `model.world.shape`, `model.light`, `model.camera`, `model.perspective`, `model.material`, `model.texture` |
| **Display** | `view` |
| **Geometry building blocks** | `model.world.triangle`, `math.transform` |
| **Math library** | `math`, `math.vector`, `math.projection`, `math.tools` |
| **Utilities** | `tools.color`, `tools.tracing` |

### S4. Images and diagrams

- Copy the images of `docs/images` into `doc-files` folders (next to the `package-info.java` files, or
  under `src/main/javadoc/doc-files` for the home page): renderings of the gallery, lighting, `UrbanScape`.
- The **Mermaid** diagrams of DESIGN (architecture, pipeline, contexts, extension points) are not interpreted by
  Javadoc. The simplest and most durable: export them once as SVG (`mermaid-cli`) into `doc-files`. Loading Mermaid
  in JavaScript (`--add-script`) is possible, but makes the Javadoc depend on an external script, including in the
  `-javadoc` jar.
- The existing ASCII diagrams (view volume of `Perspective`, cone of `SpotLight`, `Torus`) are useful and didactic:
  putting them in `<pre>` (escaping `<` and `>`) is enough, see C1.

## 4. Content of the comments (C)

### C1. Fix the 72 errors — mechanical, ½ day

- ASCII diagrams and formulas → `<pre>…</pre>`, with `&lt;` and `&gt;` (or `{@code}` in running text).
- `@date` (6 classes of `math.vector`) → remove, or `@since` (see A2).
- 26 `@param` whose name no longer matches the signature → rename.
- Dashed lists → `<ul><li>`; paragraphs separated by `<p>`.

### C2. A writing rule (to be added to DESIGN §12)

A 3D rendering API has recurring questions that each comment must answer when they apply. Today they are scattered
(or missing):

1. **First sentence**: what the method does or what the class is, in the 3rd person ("Returns…", "Renders…"). It is
   the only sentence visible in the tables.
2. **Coordinate space**: world, frame of the element, camera, clip, NDC, screen. It is the first source of errors in
   3D, and the pipeline already names them (DESIGN §4).
3. **Units and conventions**: world units or pixels, angles in radians or degrees, Z up, direction of a vector
   (towards the scene or towards the light), counterclockwise winding seen from outside.
4. **Mutation or new object**: the math library is "half immutable" (performance audit, D5). Each method must say
   whether it changes `this` or returns a new object, and whether the result can be changed safely (the accessors
   `xAxis()` already do this very well).
5. **`null`**: accepted? meaning what? ("`null` inherits from the parent element", contract C8 of the cookbook).
6. **Life cycle**: to be called before or after `build()`, once per frame, etc.
7. **Exceptions**: `@throws` for the declared exceptions (34 already present) and for the `IllegalStateException`
   of the immutable presets of `RenderContext`.
8. **Links**: `{@link}` to the classes mentioned, `{@code}` for code, `@see` to the complementary method.

The Java 9+ tags `@apiNote` (advice on use), `@implSpec` (contract for a subclass) and `@implNote` (implementation
detail) suit a didactic project well: they separate what the user must know from what explains the algorithm,
without removing anything. They are turned on with three `<tags>` in the plugin.

### C3. Document the path of the user first

Rather than aiming at 100% everywhere, follow the path of a user, in this order:

| Priority | Classes | Source of the content |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Render a scene | `RenderEngine`, `World`, `Camera`, `Lighting`, `ImageView`, `SwingView` | README "Hello, Aventura", "How it works" |
| 2. Configure | `RenderContext` (options, presets, `RenderingType`), `PerspectiveContext`, `PerspectiveType` | README "Rendering options", DESIGN §8 |
| 3. Populate the scene | `Element`, the 16 shapes of `model.world.shape`, `Texture`, `SolidMaterial`, `TexturedMaterial` | README, cookbook §1 and §3 |
| 4. Light | `AmbientLight`, `DirectionalLight`, `PointLight`, `SpotLight`, `ShadowingLight` | DESIGN §6 and §7, README "Lights and shadows" |
| 5. Extend | `GenerativeElement`, `Material`, `FragmentConsumer`, `Fragment`, `GUIView`, `Light` | DESIGN §9, cookbook §2 (contracts C1 to C10) |
| 6. Mathematics | complete `math.transform`, `math.projection`, `math.tools` | unit tests |

The **contracts C1 to C10 of the cookbook** naturally belong in the Javadoc of `GenerativeElement` (with
`@implSpec` on `generateVertices()` and `generateTriangles()`): that is where someone who writes a shape looks for
them. The cookbook keeps the detailed recipes and refers to the Javadoc for the contracts.

### C4. Tested examples with `{@snippet}`

`{@snippet}` includes a region of a compiled class, instead of copying code into a comment:

```java
/**
 * ...
 * {@snippet class=com.aventura.cookbook.PyramidFrustum region=vertices}
 */
```

The examples already exist in `src/test/java` and are checked by `mvn test`:

| Example | Where to include it |
|---|---|
| `demo.HelloAventura` | `overview.html`, `RenderEngine` |
| `cookbook.PyramidFrustum` | `GenerativeElement` (new shape) |
| `cookbook.ClosedConeFrustum` | `GenerativeElement` (enrich by inheritance) |
| `cookbook.StreetLamp` | `Element` (assembly, pivot, sub-elements) |
| presets of `RenderContext` (README) | `RenderContext` |

Adding `// @start region=…` / `// @end` markers in these classes is enough. Short inline snippets
(`{@snippet : … }`) are enough for simple methods.

### C5. The known traps, written where one falls into them

`BACKLOG.md` and DESIGN list traps that the user cannot guess. As long as they are not fixed, they must appear in
the Javadoc (`@apiNote` or a "<b>Note:</b>" paragraph):

- `PerspectiveContext`: the `(int, int, …)` overload is in **pixels**, `(float, float, …)` in **units**; the order
  `(top, bottom, right, left, far, near)` differs from that of `Perspective`; the size in pixels is set at
  construction (BACKLOG §1).
- `ShadowingLight(int)` (type of box) and `ShadowingLight(float)` (intensity) are easily confused;
  `SHADOWING_BOX_ELEMENT` and `SHADOWING_BOX_SPECIFIC` fall back to `SHADOWING_BOX_WORLD` (BACKLOG §3).
- `Triangle.setRectoVerso()` and `Vertex.setColor()` have no effect on the rendering (BACKLOG §5).
- Never keep a `Fragment` after `consume()` (DESIGN §12).
- The texture paths are relative to the working directory (DESIGN §12, "Known limitations").

### C6. Take the history out of the comments

43 passages describe the history of the code rather than its use: "CHANGED BEHAVIOR: this used to…"
(`DirectionalLight`), "the former Rasterizer façade", "Legacy-parity constants", "formerly on…". They are valuable
to the author but confusing for a reader of the API. Proposal: keep **the current behavior** in the Javadoc (with a
short `@apiNote` if needed), and move the story to a `CHANGELOG.md` or to the commit messages. The internal `//`
comments can stay as they are: they do not appear in the Javadoc.

## 5. API surface (A)

What the Javadoc shows is what is `public` or `protected`. A few elements displayed today should not be part of the
API, or need a decision.

### A1. Mutable public fields

19 `public static` fields that are not `final`, visible to and changeable by any user:

- ~~`Vector3.nb_vectors`, `Vector4.nb_vectors`, `nb_to_display`~~: instrumentation counters, **removed** (October
  2026, performance audit D1).
- `Light.DEFAULT_LIGHT_INTENSITY`: a constant that is **not `final`**, which a user can change for the whole engine.
  To be made `final`.
- The flags of `Tracer` (`function`, `error`, `exception`…): to be hidden behind methods, or taken out of the public
  API.

### A2. `@since` and `@deprecated`

- `@since` holds dates ("May 2016", "Nov 2023", "2026"…). In an API, `@since` gives the **version** from which an
  element exists. Proposal: remove the current dates (the history is in git) and use `@since 0.1` from the first
  published version.
- A single `@deprecated` (`Vector2`): well written, but to be accompanied by `@Deprecated(forRemoval = true)` and a
  `{@link}` to its replacement.

### A3. Tell the user API from the internals of the engine

`engine` exposes as `public` some internal classes of the pipeline (`ElementTransform`, `ViewProjection`,
`NearPlaneClipper`, `ZBuffer`, `TriangleRasterizer`, the consumers…), and the `-protected` option displays about
200 undocumented `protected` fields (`light_vector`, components of the vectors…). Three options, from the lightest
to the most structuring:

1. **Document the status**: an "Internal: part of the rendering pipeline, not needed to render a scene" paragraph
   in their Javadoc, and a separate "Rendering pipeline (internals)" group.
2. **Reduce the visibility** where possible (`protected` fields → `private` + accessor, classes → package-private),
   along with the refactorings of the performance audit (D4, D9).
3. **`module-info.java`** exporting only the API packages: the Javadoc no longer shows the rest. It is the cleanest
   solution, but it requires reorganizing `engine` (public API on one side, pipeline on the other).

For a didactic project, option 1 is enough in the short term: the internals stay visible to whoever wants to learn,
but the user knows they can be ignored.

| README | The scene and the engine | `overview.html`, `RenderEngine` |
| README | Packages (table) | first sentence of the 19 `package-info.java` |
| README | Rendering options, presets | `RenderContext`, `RenderingType`, `package-info` of `context` |
| README | Lights and shadows | `package-info` of `model.light` |
| README, DESIGN | Building your own geometry, §9 Extension points | `overview.html`, `GenerativeElement`, `Material`, `FragmentConsumer`, `GUIView`, `Light` |
| DESIGN | §2 Architecture (diagram) | `overview.html` (SVG) and groups (S3) |
| DESIGN | §4 Pipeline, coordinates, one frame step by step | `package-info` of `engine` |
| DESIGN | §5 Rasterization and fragments | `TriangleRasterizer`, `Fragment`, `FragmentConsumer` |
| DESIGN | §6 Lighting model, kinds of lights | `model.light`, each light class |
| DESIGN | §7 Shadow mapping | `ShadowingLight` |
| DESIGN | §8 The two contexts | `RenderContext`, `PerspectiveContext` |
| DESIGN | §12 Conventions | `overview.html` ("Conventions" section) |
| Cookbook | §1 The model in five minutes | `package-info` of `model.world` |
| Cookbook | §2 Contracts C1–C10 | `GenerativeElement`, `Element` (`@implSpec`) |
| Cookbook | §3 Toolbox | `package-info` of `model.world.triangle` and `math.transform` |
| Cookbook | §4–§7 Recipes | `{@snippet}` of the cookbook classes, link to the cookbook |
| Cookbook | §10 Known problems of the shapes | `Sphere` (winding, normals) |
| BACKLOG | §1, §3, §5 | `@apiNote` of the traps (C5) |
| Performance audit | D1, D5 | A1, C2 (mutation or new object) |

The principle: **the Javadoc says what to use and how, DESIGN and the cookbook say why and how it is built**, and
each refers to the other. This avoids maintaining the same text twice.

## 7. Proposed roadmap

### Phase 0 — Make the site presentable (½ day, mechanical)

| # | Action | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| J1 | License as `/* */` at the top of the file (script on the 100 files) | readable summary tables everywhere |
| J2 | MIT footer | consistent with the license |
| J4 | Exclude `demo`, `author=false`, title | index centered on the API |
| C1 | Fix the 72 errors (`<pre>`, `@date`, `@param`) | readable diagrams |
| J3 | `doclint all,-missing`, `failOnError=true` | no more regressions |

### Phase 1 — Structure (½ to 1 day, mostly moving text)

| # | Action |
|---|---|
| S1 | `overview.html`: tagline, Hello Aventura as `{@snippet}`, diagram, reading order, conventions |
| S2 | 19 `package-info.java` from the README and DESIGN |
| S3 | Package groups |
| S4 | `doc-files`: images of the gallery, Mermaid diagrams exported as SVG |

At this stage, the Javadoc is already a real entry point to the engine.

### Phase 2 — The path of the user (2 to 3 days, spread over time)

| # | Action |
|---|---|
| C2 | Writing rule added to DESIGN §12 |
| C3 | Priorities 1 to 4: `RenderEngine`, `World`, contexts, shapes, lights, views |
| C4 | `{@snippet}` of the cookbook classes and of the presets |
| C5 | Known traps as `@apiNote` |
| C6 | History moved to `CHANGELOG.md` |

### Phase 3 — Extension and finishing touches (1 to 2 days)

| # | Action |
|---|---|
| C3 | Priorities 5 and 6: extension points (`@implSpec`), math library |
| A1 | Mutable public fields (together with D1 of the performance audit) |
| A2 | `@since` as versions, `@Deprecated(forRemoval = true)` |
| A3 | "Internal" status of the pipeline classes, separate group |
| J3 | `doclint all` + `failOnWarnings` in continuous integration |

### Phase 4 — Optional

- Publish the Javadoc on **GitHub Pages** (or javadoc.io once on Maven Central) and link it from the README.
- A light style sheet (`--add-stylesheet`) in the colors of the project.
- `module-info.java` (A3, option 3), to be coordinated with phase 2 of the performance audit (D9).
- Comments in Markdown (`///`, Java 23+) if the project moves one day to a more recent JDK: more pleasant to write,
  but not necessary.

Each phase is validated by generating the Javadoc again (`mvn javadoc:javadoc`) and opening
`target/reports/apidocs/index.html`: home page, a package page, `RenderEngine`, `Sphere`, `RenderContext`.

---

## 8. What not to do

- **Generate comments automatically** ("@param x the x") to make the warnings disappear: the count goes down, the
  documentation is no better, and these empty comments hide the ones that are really missing.
- **Aim at 100% from the start**: the obvious accessors (`getX()`) and the internal classes can wait. The path of
  the user (C3) first.
- **Copy DESIGN or the cookbook into the Javadoc**: link, summarize, and include the code with `{@snippet}`.
- **Remove the didactic explanations** (ASCII diagrams, GPU equivalent, reasons for an algorithm): they make the
  value of the project. Format them (`<pre>`) and, if they describe the implementation rather than the use, put them
  under `@implNote`.
- **Leave `doclint none`** once the cleanup is done: without an automatic check, the Javadoc degrades with every
  refactoring (the 26 obsolete `@param` show it).
